tasks.short: Develop visual concepts and sample layouts for commercial briefs.

steps.what: Read the brief, brand guidance, approved copy and channel requirements.

loop.input: Design brief, brand guidelines, approved copy and channel specifications.
loop.output: Design constraints with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields; designer checks source passages and conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved conflicts return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text briefs express priorities and restrictions inconsistently.

steps.what: Sketch alternative compositions in graphics software in the {OTHER}.

loop.input: Design constraints, approved assets and editable layout components.
loop.output: A small set of editable concept layouts.
loop.check: Check dimensions, required copy and asset use; designer judges hierarchy and originality.
loop.stop: Generate three candidates and allow one revision round; designer sketches missing directions manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle established formats, but this step explores new visual compositions.

steps.what: Compare concepts and choose a direction against the brief.
Refine typography, spacing and composition in graphics software in the {OTHER}.
Review the proof and approve the visual direction.
File the approved layout and update the project status.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {PROJECT} links to approved assets and guidance in the {DOCS}; a bounded loop extracts constraints and drafts editable concepts in graphics software in the {OTHER}. The designer selects and refines the direction, while the {WORKFLOW} routes proof approval and files the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, assets and feedback were disconnected. Bespoke composition still required substantial manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Editable concept generation is available, and AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting briefs, assets and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive composition, typography and coherent brand expression need experienced judgement. Generated concepts can converge on familiar visual patterns.
tasks.human_edge: The designer turns ambiguous commercial aims into a visual idea and recognises when an attractive layout communicates the wrong message.

ambition.what: A concept comparison session showing three genuinely different visual directions before production.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time assembling first drafts and more time developing and explaining visual directions. Marketing retains final approval; any delegated concept-selection authority must be agreed.

reach.task: Translate campaign objectives into concept evaluation criteria.
reach.learn: Audience priorities, campaign economics and how creative decisions support the intended response.

evidence.claim: Figma Make produces editable prototypes from prompts and a team's design system; suitability for each graphic format needs testing.
Figma Buzz supports locked template areas and spreadsheet-driven variants for established formats.
The supplied research reports higher output and ratings alongside lower average novelty among text-to-image adopters.
The proposed workflow, time allocation and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The baseline is a mixed in-house marketing design team with reusable brand assets.
Creation mainly happens on screen; the meeting-heavy prior overstates meetings for this task.
Concept approval is separate from permission to publish or place a print order.
Build ranges assume one pilot team and include access review and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Whether approved assets and brand components are complete and consistently versioned.
Whether the graphics software in the {OTHER} exposes editable formats or supported interfaces.
Who can approve visual direction and which decisions the designer may make independently.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed workflow.
research_questions: Can generated concepts remain editable without losing typography or component structure?
Does concept generation produce materially different directions on representative briefs?
Which established formats can use configured templates without a model loop?
new_work: Check extracted constraints against their sources.
Maintain approved components, templates and source links.
Monitor revision effort and approval delays during rollout.

tasks.short: Create and finish new digital images for marketing use.

steps.what: Define the subject, composition and intended use from the design brief.
Find approved reference images and check their permitted uses.
Construct candidate images in image-editing software in the {OTHER}.

loop.input: Image specification and references cleared for the intended processing and use.
loop.output: Candidate images with generation history and available provenance metadata.
loop.check: Check dimensions and metadata; designer inspects visual defects, factual fidelity and brief fit.
loop.stop: Two batches of four candidates maximum; switch to manual construction if neither batch works.
loop.why_not_simpler: New subjects and compositions cannot be produced through resizing or fixed templates alone.

steps.what: Select and retouch a candidate in image-editing software in the {OTHER}.
Approve the image for its stated marketing use.
Export delivery files and archive the approved master.

tasks.design: Approved references and usage records in the {DOCS} feed a bounded image-generation loop in image-editing software in the {OTHER}. The designer selects and retouches candidates; deterministic exports create channel files and preserve available provenance, with approval recorded through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creating each image required substantial manual construction. References, rights records and output versions were often stored separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Image generation and editing are established capabilities. Export scripts and structured asset records can connect them without autonomous agents.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate products, faces, text and consistent subjects across images remain demanding. Provenance metadata does not establish copyright ownership or clear third-party rights.
tasks.human_edge: The designer recognises misleading imagery, selects a compelling composition and finishes details that determine credibility.

ambition.what: A bounded custom-image service for internal event planners whose briefs previously received stock imagery.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time constructing initial images and more time directing, selecting and finishing them. Approval and publication rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Develop event imagery across invitations, signage and presentation screens.
reach.learn: Viewing distances, venue constraints, event milestones and attendee accessibility needs.

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images and attaches Content Credentials describing generation provenance.
A reported court decision denied copyright protection to three generated logos; it does not settle rights for every image workflow.
EU AI Act transparency duties distinguish machine-readable marking from disclosure obligations for particular uses.
The bounded generation budget and remaining-time estimates require validation on representative image briefs.

assumptions: This task concerns marketing imagery, with logos and legally sensitive depictions escalated for specialist review.
Most creation time is spent in software; the meeting-heavy prior does not fit this task.
Reference retrieval uses existing metadata and licence fields, without face recognition.
Access estimates include review of processing terms, personal data and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which reference assets may be submitted to an image-generation service.
Whether customer contracts require exclusive rights or prohibit generated imagery.
Whether provenance survives the actual export and publishing chain.
Which images depict identifiable people or confidential products.
research_questions: Which brief categories consistently yield usable candidates within the fixed generation budget?
Can export automation preserve required machine-readable marking and archive provenance?
Which image categories need manual production because factual fidelity dominates?
new_work: Inspect generated candidates for defects and misleading details.
Maintain reference permissions and generation records.
Check applicable disclosure requirements for the intended use.
Maintain export profiles and test provenance preservation.

tasks.short: Prepare approved artwork as reliable, printer-ready digital files.

steps.what: Collect the approved artwork and the printer's production requirements.
Set bleed, colour and font options in prepress software in the {OTHER}; export.
Check resolution, fonts, colours and page geometry in prepress software in the {OTHER}.
Correct preflight issues and re-export in prepress software in the {OTHER}.
Inspect the final proof for clipping, colour changes and unintended content changes.
Approve release of the final file to the printer.
Send the released file to the printer and retain the delivery receipt.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles approved artwork from the {DOCS} and selects a validated printer profile in prepress software in the {OTHER}. Configured export, preflight and safe correction rules produce a proof and issue report; after human release approval, the exact approved file is delivered through the {EMAIL} and its receipt archived.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printer specifications were scattered across messages, and export settings depended on individual memory. Existing preflight capabilities were not consistently configured or connected to release approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Profile-based preflight and correction already exist. Faster integration work makes reliable job packaging, approval binding and delivery practical.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual substrates, spot colours, finishing and colour-critical work need specialist judgement and sometimes physical proofs. Missing image detail cannot be restored by passing technical checks.
tasks.human_edge: The designer sees whether technically valid output still preserves the intended appearance and knows when to involve the printer.

ambition.what: A self-service print-readiness check for event planners submitting approved signage.

tasks.altitude: The designer handles unusual production problems and visual proofing while routine files pass through configured checks. Delegated release authority may expand for defined low-cost print categories, if agreed.

reach.task: Resolve production-file defects before printer handoff.
reach.learn: Colour profiles, font embedding, overprint, trapping and finishing requirements.

evidence.claim: Enfocus PitStop Pro checks PDFs against PDF/X profiles, applies action-list corrections and reports issues.
Configured preflight can automate much routine preparation despite the task's human-class prior.
Binding release approval to a specific file version prevents subsequent edits from inheriting approval.

assumptions: Most work uses recurring printers and a limited set of production specifications.
Safe corrections are explicitly listed; other defects stop the workflow for manual resolution.
The release gate authorises delivery of one exact file and does not authorise a new purchase.
Ranges include printer-profile validation, access and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which printer profiles, finishing methods and physical proofs are required.
Whether current prepress licences support unattended processing.
Who holds print-release authority and whether it varies by spend.
How printers accept files and return delivery receipts.
research_questions: Which historical print defects are detectable by available preflight profiles?
Which automatic fixes preserve appearance across representative production files?
Can existing software perform the complete routine path through configuration alone?
new_work: Maintain printer profiles and approved correction lists.
Investigate failed checks and unexpected visual changes.
Validate profiles when printers or production processes change.
Check that delivery always uses the approved file version.

tasks.short: Discuss layout needs with clients and agree a workable design direction.

steps.what: Review the brief, earlier feedback and layout options before the discussion.

loop.input: Current brief, layout proof notes and the relevant feedback thread.
loop.output: A source-linked agenda of open questions, constraints and contradictory requests.
loop.check: Designer checks each issue against the source and removes unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous points remain questions for the meeting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client intent and conflicting preferences are expressed in free text.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and share the current proof.
Explain audience needs, preferences and practical constraints.
Explain layout trade-offs, challenge conflicts and explore alternatives with the client.
Agree the direction, requested changes and unresolved decisions.
Write a recap of decisions, changes, responsibilities and open questions.

loop.input: Designer-entered meeting notes, explicit decisions and agreed changes.
loop.output: A recap separating agreed actions from unresolved questions.
loop.check: Designer verifies commitments, owners and dates against the notes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing details stay blank or become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes require interpretation to become a clear client-facing recap.

steps.what: Check and send the recap to the client.
Record agreed changes and update the project tasks.

tasks.design: A bounded preparation loop reads the current brief and relevant feedback from the {DOCS}, {PROJECT} and {EMAIL}, while the {CALENDAR} handles routine scheduling. The conversation and agreement stay human; a second bounded loop drafts the recap from designer notes, and the {WORKFLOW} sends the approved recap and records structured actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions were embedded in conversations and email threads. Scheduling, recaps and project updates were handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction and drafting can work from selected source material. Existing scheduling and workflow configuration can handle the surrounding administration.
tasks.still_hard: Clients may disagree internally or express preferences indirectly. A summary cannot establish agreement that was never reached.
tasks.human_edge: The designer builds trust, notices hesitation and helps clients choose between competing aims without promising an unworkable solution.

ambition.what: A pre-design alignment workshop for internal teams commissioning their first campaign.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time preparing and documenting discussions and more time resolving ambiguity with clients. Commercial commitments and client approval rights remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Align stakeholders on campaign priorities before creative production.
reach.learn: Stakeholder facilitation, scope negotiation and the campaign approval process.

evidence.claim: Client advice, feasibility discussion and final selection remain human; preparation and documentation can be handled separately.
Source-linked extraction and bounded recap drafting are feasible patterns, but the digest supplies no measured case for this meeting workflow.
GDPR applies when client correspondence or meeting notes contain personal data.

assumptions: Client includes internal commissioning teams as well as external clients.
Scheduling uses a designer-selected participant list and approved availability windows.
The workflow uses designer notes and does not require meeting recording.
Each recap stores structured actions so approved fields can populate project tasks without another model call.
Build ranges include access, retention review and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which client communications the preparation workflow may access.
Who may commit to scope, cost and delivery dates.
Whether informal meeting agreement is sufficient or written client approval is required.
Which retention and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration remove the routine coordination step?
Does the recap reliably distinguish a suggestion from an agreed commitment?
Which preparation fields improve the discussion enough to justify their review time?
new_work: Check agenda sources and remove irrelevant client history.
Resolve disputed or incomplete decisions with the client.
Maintain access scopes, retention settings and action templates.

role.altitude: The designer's week shifts toward visual direction, careful finishing and client alignment, with less initial construction and production administration. Wider decision rights require explicit delegation; automation alone does not confer them.
reach: Marketing Managers: connect visual choices to audience and campaign objectives.
Desktop Publishers: resolve complex production and colour issues.
Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners: develop coherent imagery across physical event formats.
Advertising and Promotions Managers: facilitate agreement before production begins.
skills_to_grow: Write clear visual constraints and evaluate distinct concept directions.
Build reusable components and deterministic export profiles.
Inspect generated imagery for factual, visual and rights-related problems.
Maintain provenance and bind approvals to exact file versions.
Facilitate client decisions and document explicit commitments.
Measure accepted-output quality and revision effort during rollout.
role.ambitious_version: A visual communication lead who runs early concept comparisons, supports underserved internal teams and resolves difficult production or stakeholder problems, backed by reusable templates and bounded generation.
